skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI images through the inference.sh CLI using FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and related image apps.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh image models for text-to-image, editing, upscaling, and image stitching.
skill.author: tul-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks and command examples, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. One low issue remains because an embedded remote image can trigger an external fetch, and intended use sends prompts or image URLs to an external AI service. No prompt injection or hidden command execution was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Host preview images through marketplace-controlled storage or remove remote Markdown image references.
Add a clear notice that prompts and image URLs are sent to inference.sh and selected hosted model providers.
Keep tool permissions limited to infsh and label optional npx installation commands as manual setup steps.

content.value_statement: Image teams need quick access to many hosted generation models. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh image workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists app identifiers for FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
Shows text-to-image examples for several hosted image models.
Shows image upscaling with the Topaz image upscaler app.
Shows stitching multiple image URLs into one combined image.
Links users to inference.sh documentation for running apps.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and login before use.
Sends prompts and image URLs to external hosted services.
Does not include local model weights or offline generation.
Model quality, pricing, and availability depend on inference.sh apps.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Directions
use_cases.description: Generate concept art, mood images, and style references across multiple image models.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Produce social media graphics, product visuals, and ad concepts from concise prompts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Create product scene mockups, upscale selected images, and stitch visual references.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Product Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a clean studio product image of [product] on [background]. Use a model suited for high quality product visuals.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three versions of [scene] using FLUX, Gemini, and Seedream. Summarize visible differences in realism, text, and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Upscale A Selected Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Upscale this image URL for a presentation. Preserve the subject, improve detail, and report the selected output size.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Multi-Step Visual Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a hero image, a square social version, and a stitched comparison board for [campaign]. Use consistent colors and composition.

output_examples.input: Create a cinematic mountain lake landscape for a travel campaign.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Seedream 4.5. Expected result: a high resolution landscape prompt ready for an inference.sh image run.

output_examples.input: Upscale this product image for an ecommerce hero.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Topaz Upscaler. Expected result: a sharper product image with preserved edges and cleaner details.

output_examples.input: Make a poster that contains the words HELLO WORLD.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Reve. Expected result: a poster prompt focused on readable text and controlled composition.

best_practices: Start with clear subject matter, lighting, composition, aspect ratio, and intended use.
Use model-specific strengths, such as Reve for text and Topaz for upscaling.
Review data sensitivity before sending prompts or image URLs to external services.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential product designs or private image URLs without approval.
Do not assume every model supports the same aspect ratios or image inputs.
Do not use vague prompts when brand, layout, or text accuracy matters.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides hosted image generation through the inference.sh CLI.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the infsh CLI, an inference.sh account, and access to selected apps.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. Editing is available when the selected app supports image-to-image, inpainting, stitching, or upscaling.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Are prompts sent to third parties?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and image URLs are processed by inference.sh and the selected hosted model.

faq.question: Which model should I choose?
faq.answer: Use FLUX for general quality, Reve for text rendering, Seedream for cinematic quality, and Topaz for upscaling.
